deities: Lord Shiva as Paramahansa Nath (Patal-Phuta Shiva linga)
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (with a large fair, reported ~15 days)

history.period: 15th century CE (reign of Prataprudra Deva; some visitor sources claim 11th c. — verify)
history.summary: The Sri Paramahansanatha Temple (Parama Hansanath) stands at Paramahansa village near Biribati, Cuttack district, northeast of Cuttack city near Choudwar — the CSV town 'Cuttack' is approximate; the temple is at Biribati, PIN 754100. It is one of the popular Shiva sanctuaries of Odisha, dated by regional sources to the 15th century during the rule of Gajapati king Prataprudra Deva (some visitor reviews claim the 11th century — verify). It is a five-chambered rekha-and-pidha complex with a pancharatha vimana; the sanctum holds a Patal-Phuta Shiva linga, and the doorjambs and plinth carry navagraha, dvarapala, war-scene, elephant and swan carvings, with subsidiary images of Parvati, Kartikeya, Ganesha, Nandi, a Rama-abhisheka panel and Vishnu figures. The temple is reported as ASI-protected, draws a large Mahashivaratri fair, and restricts photography inside the premises. CSV state Odisha is correct.

name: Paramahansa Nath Temple
town: Paramahansa, Biribati (CSV town 'Cuttack' is approximate; the temple is at Biribati, PIN 754100, northeast of Cuttack city)
town_description: Paramahansa is a village near Biribati in Cuttack district, Odisha, northeast of Cuttack city toward Choudwar and Kandarpur. The surrounding area is rural and green near the Mahanadi; Cuttack city (the 'Silver City', former Odisha capital) is the district headquarters and nearest major hub, with the famous Dhabaleswar island Shiva temple also nearby.
